newsitem.title: GERMANY: German policeman confesses in brutality trial.
newsitem.headline: German policeman confesses in brutality trial.

text.p: A German policeman confessed on Tuesday he had filmed colleagues attacking a group of skinheads and showed the video to other officers afterwards as entertainment.
Carsten Richter, a 25-year-old Berlin policeman, gave his testimony on the first day of a trial in which 16 officers are accused of brutality against suspects or of turning a blind eye to abuse.
Richter said he had shown the video of the skinheads, who had been detained for rioting on New Year's Eve, 1993, to other officers in his precinct, who had reacted with amusement.
"I regretted it later," Richter told the court but added in his defence that he had felt pressured by a "dominant, hard-core" group of older officers to take part in such attacks.
The 16 officers are accused of beating suspects with their fists or truncheons or watching such attacks in 12 cases between October 1993 and May 1994.
Prosecutors allege Vietnamese and Poles were also among the victims.
